options.content: **Reply-path latency.** The `recall:*` phases below run in `before_prompt`, *before the LLM is called*, so their duration is added directly to how long Jarvis takes to reply. The `routine:*` table at the bottom is **background scheduled work — not in the reply path**; those multi-minute spans do not delay your messages. The signal to watch is recall latency and how often it crosses 2s/5s.

panels.title: Recall latency by phase (reply-path, before LLM)
panels.description: Duration of each before_prompt recall phase per turn. These run before the model is invoked, so they add directly to perceived reply time. user_profile is usually cache-served (~1ms); procedural and knowledge carry embedding + HyDE + query-augmentation + Graphiti cost and are the main contributors.

targets.rawQueryText: SELECT CAST(strftime('%s',ts) AS INTEGER) AS time, json_extract(detail,'$.name') AS metric, json_extract(detail,'$.durationMs') AS value FROM agent_events WHERE event='perf_span' AND json_extract(detail,'$.name') LIKE 'recall:%' AND julianday(ts) >= julianday($__from/1000,'unixepoch') AND julianday(ts) < julianday($__to/1000,'unixepoch') ORDER BY time
targets.queryText: SELECT CAST(strftime('%s',ts) AS INTEGER) AS time, json_extract(detail,'$.name') AS metric, json_extract(detail,'$.durationMs') AS value FROM agent_events WHERE event='perf_span' AND json_extract(detail,'$.name') LIKE 'recall:%' AND julianday(ts) >= julianday($__from/1000,'unixepoch') AND julianday(ts) < julianday($__to/1000,'unixepoch') ORDER BY time

panels.title: Slow recalls per hour (>2s, >5s)
panels.description: How often a before_prompt recall phase crossed 2s (amber) and 5s (red), bucketed hourly. This is the frequency of visibly-slow replies. A flat low line means recall is staying fast; spikes mark the windows worth investigating.

targets.rawQueryText: SELECT CAST((strftime('%s',ts)/3600)*3600 AS INTEGER) AS time, COUNT(*) AS value FROM agent_events WHERE event='perf_span' AND json_extract(detail,'$.name') LIKE 'recall:%' AND json_extract(detail,'$.durationMs') > 2000 AND julianday(ts) >= julianday($__from/1000,'unixepoch') AND julianday(ts) < julianday($__to/1000,'unixepoch') GROUP BY time ORDER BY time
targets.queryText: SELECT CAST((strftime('%s',ts)/3600)*3600 AS INTEGER) AS time, COUNT(*) AS value FROM agent_events WHERE event='perf_span' AND json_extract(detail,'$.name') LIKE 'recall:%' AND json_extract(detail,'$.durationMs') > 2000 AND julianday(ts) >= julianday($__from/1000,'unixepoch') AND julianday(ts) < julianday($__to/1000,'unixepoch') GROUP BY time ORDER BY time

targets.queryText: SELECT CAST((strftime('%s',ts)/3600)*3600 AS INTEGER) AS time, COUNT(*) AS value FROM agent_events WHERE event='perf_span' AND json_extract(detail,'$.name') LIKE 'recall:%' AND json_extract(detail,'$.durationMs') > 5000 AND julianday(ts) >= julianday($__from/1000,'unixepoch') AND julianday(ts) < julianday($__to/1000,'unixepoch') GROUP BY time ORDER BY time

panels.title: Recall phase stats (selected range)
panels.description: Per-phase recall cost over the dashboard time range: call count, average and max duration, and how many calls exceeded 2s. Ranks which recall phase is the dominant reply-path cost.

targets.rawQueryText: SELECT json_extract(detail,'$.name') AS phase, COUNT(*) AS n, ROUND(AVG(json_extract(detail,'$.durationMs'))) AS avg_ms, MAX(json_extract(detail,'$.durationMs')) AS max_ms, SUM(CASE WHEN json_extract(detail,'$.durationMs')>2000 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS over_2s FROM agent_events WHERE event='perf_span' AND json_extract(detail,'$.name') LIKE 'recall:%' AND julianday(ts) >= julianday($__from/1000,'unixepoch') AND julianday(ts) < julianday($__to/1000,'unixepoch') GROUP BY phase ORDER BY avg_ms DESC
targets.queryText: SELECT json_extract(detail,'$.name') AS phase, COUNT(*) AS n, ROUND(AVG(json_extract(detail,'$.durationMs'))) AS avg_ms, MAX(json_extract(detail,'$.durationMs')) AS max_ms, SUM(CASE WHEN json_extract(detail,'$.durationMs')>2000 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS over_2s FROM agent_events WHERE event='perf_span' AND json_extract(detail,'$.name') LIKE 'recall:%' AND julianday(ts) >= julianday($__from/1000,'unixepoch') AND julianday(ts) < julianday($__to/1000,'unixepoch') GROUP BY phase ORDER BY avg_ms DESC

panels.title: Memory write latency — extractAndStore (turn_end, post-reply)
panels.description: Duration of the post-turn fact extraction/store pass. This fires AFTER the reply is delivered (turns 4, 7, 10... and session_end), so it does not delay the current reply — but it competes for CPU/embeddings and can slow a rapid follow-up. Watch for growth.

targets.rawQueryText: SELECT CAST(strftime('%s',ts) AS INTEGER) AS time, json_extract(detail,'$.durationMs') AS value FROM agent_events WHERE event='perf_span' AND json_extract(detail,'$.name')='extractAndStore' AND julianday(ts) >= julianday($__from/1000,'unixepoch') AND julianday(ts) < julianday($__to/1000,'unixepoch') ORDER BY time
targets.queryText: SELECT CAST(strftime('%s',ts) AS INTEGER) AS time, json_extract(detail,'$.durationMs') AS value FROM agent_events WHERE event='perf_span' AND json_extract(detail,'$.name')='extractAndStore' AND julianday(ts) >= julianday($__from/1000,'unixepoch') AND julianday(ts) < julianday($__to/1000,'unixepoch') ORDER BY time

panels.title: Background routines (NOT reply-path) — duration
panels.description: Scheduled background routines and their durations. These run on the scheduler, independent of your messages, so their multi-minute spans do NOT delay replies. Shown to keep them visible (and distinct from reply-path cost) and to catch a runaway routine.

targets.rawQueryText: SELECT json_extract(detail,'$.name') AS routine, COUNT(*) AS n, ROUND(AVG(json_extract(detail,'$.durationMs'))) AS avg_ms, MAX(json_extract(detail,'$.durationMs')) AS max_ms FROM agent_events WHERE event='perf_span' AND json_extract(detail,'$.name') LIKE 'routine:%' AND julianday(ts) >= julianday($__from/1000,'unixepoch') AND julianday(ts) < julianday($__to/1000,'unixepoch') GROUP BY routine ORDER BY avg_ms DESC
targets.queryText: SELECT json_extract(detail,'$.name') AS routine, COUNT(*) AS n, ROUND(AVG(json_extract(detail,'$.durationMs'))) AS avg_ms, MAX(json_extract(detail,'$.durationMs')) AS max_ms FROM agent_events WHERE event='perf_span' AND json_extract(detail,'$.name') LIKE 'routine:%' AND julianday(ts) >= julianday($__from/1000,'unixepoch') AND julianday(ts) < julianday($__to/1000,'unixepoch') GROUP BY routine ORDER BY avg_ms DESC

panels.title: TOTAL turn latency (end-to-end, what you feel)
panels.description: Full turn wall-clock for the interactive Sonnet-via-CLI session (perf_metrics 'llm' phase): from before_prompt to turn_end, including the model call and any in-turn staff dispatch. This is the number that matches 'Jarvis takes 10-25s'. Recall is only a small slice of it; the rest is the model turn (and dispatched sub-agents).

targets.rawQueryText: SELECT CAST(strftime('%s',created_at) AS INTEGER) AS time, latency_ms AS value FROM perf_metrics WHERE phase='llm' AND julianday(created_at) >= julianday($__from/1000,'unixepoch') AND julianday(created_at) < julianday($__to/1000,'unixepoch') ORDER BY time
targets.queryText: SELECT CAST(strftime('%s',created_at) AS INTEGER) AS time, latency_ms AS value FROM perf_metrics WHERE phase='llm' AND julianday(created_at) >= julianday($__from/1000,'unixepoch') AND julianday(created_at) < julianday($__to/1000,'unixepoch') ORDER BY time

panels.title: Per-turn injected size (approx tokens)
panels.description: What the harness injects every turn: the before_prompt system prompt (SOUL + memory + staff catalog + ...) and the context_inject block. More input tokens means a slower model turn. This is the measured driver candidate for general slowness — watch it against total turn latency above.

targets.rawQueryText: SELECT CAST(strftime('%s',ts) AS INTEGER) AS time, json_extract(detail,'$.approxTokens') AS value FROM agent_events WHERE event='prompt_size' AND julianday(ts) >= julianday($__from/1000,'unixepoch') AND julianday(ts) < julianday($__to/1000,'unixepoch') ORDER BY time
targets.queryText: SELECT CAST(strftime('%s',ts) AS INTEGER) AS time, json_extract(detail,'$.approxTokens') AS value FROM agent_events WHERE event='prompt_size' AND julianday(ts) >= julianday($__from/1000,'unixepoch') AND julianday(ts) < julianday($__to/1000,'unixepoch') ORDER BY time

targets.rawQueryText: SELECT CAST(strftime('%s',ts) AS INTEGER) AS time, json_extract(detail,'$.approxTokens') AS value FROM agent_events WHERE event='context_size' AND julianday(ts) >= julianday($__from/1000,'unixepoch') AND julianday(ts) < julianday($__to/1000,'unixepoch') ORDER BY time
targets.queryText: SELECT CAST(strftime('%s',ts) AS INTEGER) AS time, json_extract(detail,'$.approxTokens') AS value FROM agent_events WHERE event='context_size' AND julianday(ts) >= julianday($__from/1000,'unixepoch') AND julianday(ts) < julianday($__to/1000,'unixepoch') ORDER BY time

panels.title: Staff dispatch duration (in-turn sub-agents)
panels.description: Wall-clock of each interactive staff dispatch (agent_start to agent_end), e.g. the mail-triage staffer for an email question. This runs inside the turn, so it is the slice of a slow reply spent in a sub-agent. Empty until the next dispatch fires post-deploy.

targets.rawQueryText: SELECT CAST(strftime('%s',ts) AS INTEGER) AS time, json_extract(detail,'$.name') AS metric, json_extract(detail,'$.durationMs') AS value FROM agent_events WHERE event='perf_span' AND json_extract(detail,'$.name') LIKE 'dispatch:%' AND julianday(ts) >= julianday($__from/1000,'unixepoch') AND julianday(ts) < julianday($__to/1000,'unixepoch') ORDER BY time
targets.queryText: SELECT CAST(strftime('%s',ts) AS INTEGER) AS time, json_extract(detail,'$.name') AS metric, json_extract(detail,'$.durationMs') AS value FROM agent_events WHERE event='perf_span' AND json_extract(detail,'$.name') LIKE 'dispatch:%' AND julianday(ts) >= julianday($__from/1000,'unixepoch') AND julianday(ts) < julianday($__to/1000,'unixepoch') ORDER BY time

panels.title: Recall cache hit rate (%/hour)
panels.description: Share of turns served from the in-session profile/procedural cache vs a fresh fetch, bucketed hourly (recall_cache event). Low hit rate = most turns pay full recall. Measured directly now, not inferred from vecMs.

targets.rawQueryText: SELECT CAST((strftime('%s',ts)/3600)*3600 AS INTEGER) AS time, 100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN json_extract(detail,'$.hit')=1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/COUNT(*) AS value FROM agent_events WHERE event='recall_cache' AND julianday(ts) >= julianday($__from/1000,'unixepoch') AND julianday(ts) < julianday($__to/1000,'unixepoch') GROUP BY time ORDER BY time
targets.queryText: SELECT CAST((strftime('%s',ts)/3600)*3600 AS INTEGER) AS time, 100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN json_extract(detail,'$.hit')=1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/COUNT(*) AS value FROM agent_events WHERE event='recall_cache' AND julianday(ts) >= julianday($__from/1000,'unixepoch') AND julianday(ts) < julianday($__to/1000,'unixepoch') GROUP BY time ORDER BY time

panels.title: System-prompt breakdown (latest turn, chars)
panels.description: Where the latest before_prompt system prompt's bytes came from — SOUL vs recalled memory vs procedural vs graph. Pinpoints which block to trim if the injected size turns out to be the latency driver.

targets.rawQueryText: SELECT json_extract(detail,'$.systemPromptChars') AS total, json_extract(detail,'$.soulChars') AS soul, json_extract(detail,'$.memoryChars') AS memory, json_extract(detail,'$.proceduralChars') AS procedural, json_extract(detail,'$.graphChars') AS graph FROM agent_events WHERE event='prompt_size' ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 1
targets.queryText: SELECT json_extract(detail,'$.systemPromptChars') AS total, json_extract(detail,'$.soulChars') AS soul, json_extract(detail,'$.memoryChars') AS memory, json_extract(detail,'$.proceduralChars') AS procedural, json_extract(detail,'$.graphChars') AS graph FROM agent_events WHERE event='prompt_size' ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 1
